full_judgment: 2. In a suit or partition the plaintiffs who are the appellants claimed that `Ka' schedule land measuring 4 acres originally belong to Imam Bux in Raiyati right, who died leaving behind a widow Pathani Bibi, a son Sayed All and two daughters Elemjan Bibi and Halimon Bibi. Subsequently Pathani Bibi died leaving behind her aforesaid son and daughters. There was an amicable partition of the inherited property among Elemjan, Halimon and Sayed Ali. Syed Ali got 'Ga' schedule land measuring 2.07 acres out of `Ka' schedule and Elemjan and Halimon got 'Kha' schedule land measuring 1.94 acres out of `Ka' schedule. Schedule 'Gila' land was the self acquired property of the said Sayed Ali. Abdul Majid filed a partition suit being Title Suit No. 175 of 1968, in which Abdul Majid admitted about the amicable partition. Syed Ali died leaving behind a widow, Kulsum, 3 sons Wazuddin, Abdul Majid (predecessor of the defendants) and Ofazuddin and a daughter. Banesa Bibi. The aforesaid Ofazuddin died leaving behind his mother Kulsum, two brothers Wazuddin and Abdul Majid and sister Banesa. The heirs of the Sayed Ali dispossessed Elemjan and Halimon Bibi from 'Kha' schedule land against which Elemjan Bibi and Halimon Bibi filed  Title Suit No. 1225 of 1922 in the Court of 3rd Munsif, Dhaka, in which, they got decree for khas possession. Suit plot Nos. 27 and 29 were sold in auction for arrear of rent in Money Execution Case Nos. 110 and 111 of 1952. Siratunnessa and Atikullah, wife and son respectively of Abdul Majid purchased those on auction.
